# Chandras EDU

> Free engineering and professional courses with quizzes, progress tracking, and certificates (certificates are issued for the Generative AI, Computer Organization and Architecture, and Digital Logic Design courses). Part of the Chandra Shaker (chandrashaker.in) education brand.

Chandras EDU offers two course tracks: Academic engineering subjects for B.Tech students, and Professional job-readiness courses for working professionals. All content is free to read; login is required to save quiz progress and earn certificates (issued for the Generative AI, Computer Organization and Architecture, and Digital Logic Design courses).

## Academic

- [Computer Organization and Architecture](https://chandrashaker.com/courses/academic/coa/): Number systems, logic gates, combinational and sequential circuits, CPU design, memory hierarchy, and I/O organization. Pass the quiz in all 68 topics (3 out of 5 each) to earn a verifiable certificate.
- [COA Unit 1 — Number Systems & Logic](https://chandrashaker.com/courses/academic/coa/unit1/): Data types, complements, fixed/floating-point representation, binary codes, binary logic, storage registers, logic gates, and K-map representation.
- [COA Unit 2 — Combinational & Sequential Logic](https://chandrashaker.com/courses/academic/coa/unit2/): Combinational circuits, analysis and design procedure, binary/decimal adders, binary multipliers, magnitude comparators, decoders, encoders, and multiplexers, each as its own topic; plus sequential logic — SR/D/JK/T latches and flip-flops, shift registers, ring/Johnson counters, and asynchronous/synchronous counter design.
- [COA Unit 3 — Register Transfer & Basic Computer Organization](https://chandrashaker.com/courses/academic/coa/unit3/): Register transfer language, controlled register transfer hardware, bus and memory transfers, and the arithmetic/logic/shift micro-operations (plus a combined arithmetic logic shift unit) that a CPU's ALU is built from; then a complete simple computer — instruction codes, registers, the full instruction set, timing/control, the fetch-decode-execute cycle, memory-reference instruction RTL, and I/O with interrupts.
- [COA Unit 4 — Microprogrammed Control, CPU Organization & Computer Arithmetic](https://chandrashaker.com/courses/academic/coa/unit4/): Control memory, address sequencing, general register organization, stack organization, instruction formats, addressing modes, data transfer and manipulation, program control, addition and subtraction, multiplication algorithms, division algorithms, and floating-point arithmetic operations, with diagrams and quizzes.
- [COA Unit 5 — Input-Output & Memory Organization](https://chandrashaker.com/courses/academic/coa/unit5/): input-output interface, modes of transfer, priority interrupt, direct memory access, memory hierarchy, main memory, auxiliary memory, associative memory, and cache memory (mapping with worked address splits; FIFO, LRU and optimal replacement with solved problems), with diagrams and quizzes. Supplementary topics (beyond the syllabus, no quiz): virtual memory.
- [COA unit slides](https://chandrashaker.com/courses/academic/coa/): Lecture slides for each COA unit are downloadable as PDF and PowerPoint from the unit pages (free, for personal study).
- [Digital Logic Design](https://chandrashaker.com/courses/academic/dld/): Number systems and codes, error detection/correction, Boolean algebra, K-map minimization, combinational and sequential circuits, state machines, and PLDs. Pass the quiz in all 30 topics (3 out of 5 each) to earn a verifiable certificate.
- [DLD Unit 1 — Number Systems, Codes & Boolean Algebra](https://chandrashaker.com/courses/academic/dld/unit1/): Binary/octal/decimal/hex conversion, fixed/floating-point representation, 1's/2's complement, parity and Hamming error correction codes, Boolean algebra theorems, canonical forms, and the seven basic logic gates.
- [DLD Unit 2 — Gate-Level Minimization (K-Maps)](https://chandrashaker.com/courses/academic/dld/unit2/): 2/3/4-variable Karnaugh maps, SOP and POS simplification, don't-care conditions, and converting minimal expressions into NAND-NAND or NOR-NOR circuits.
- [DLD Unit 3 — Combinational Logic Circuits](https://chandrashaker.com/courses/academic/dld/unit3/): Combinational circuit analysis and design procedure, binary adder/subtractor, BCD adder and binary multiplier, magnitude comparator, decoders and encoders, and multiplexers/demultiplexers.
- [DLD Unit 4 — Sequential Logic Circuits](https://chandrashaker.com/courses/academic/dld/unit4/): Latches, flip-flops and timing (setup/hold, race-around, master-slave JK), asynchronous ripple counters, synchronous counter design, and shift registers with ring/Johnson counters.
- [DLD Unit 5 — State Machines, Memory & PLDs](https://chandrashaker.com/courses/academic/dld/unit5/): Moore vs Mealy finite state machines, state diagrams and tables, state reduction and assignment, a full FSM design worked example (overlap-aware sequence detector), programmable logic devices (ROM, PLA, PAL), memory units (RAM, ROM, decoding), and FSM case studies (traffic light, vending machine).

## Professional

- [Generative AI: Zero to Job-Ready](https://chandrashaker.com/courses/professional/genai/): A 5-module course covering GenAI foundations, prompt engineering, applied AI for developers/analysts/managers, RAG and agents, and career growth strategies; lessons end with short quizzes, and the course ends with a Final Project and a verifiable certificate.
- [AI Tools for Everyday Work](https://chandrashaker.com/courses/professional/ai-tools/): A 13-module practical course for teaching staff, office staff, and lab assistants on using free AI tools (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude) for circulars, Excel, lesson plans, lab manuals and safe/honest use. No coding needed.
